key_insight: PINNs can produce smooth, finite meniscus graphs even when no spanning equilibrium solution exists, hiding geometric incompatibility in wall-flux deficits near corners.
engineering_relevance: Capillary simulations in polygonal channels need boundary-flux checks because small interior residuals alone do not establish a physically admissible meniscus.
method: Test strong-form PINNs across the 45° square and 60° equilateral-triangle critical contact angles.
Derive a capillary-flux lower bound on combined interior and wall residual loss.
Compare with polynomial least-squares approximations under fixed sampling and optimization budgets.
evidence_signal: Several degrees below the critical angles, independently evaluated PINN losses were 1.6–1.9 times the theoretical lower bound, with polynomial least-squares results supporting the same geometric interpretation.
watch_item: The reported loss ratios apply to tested nonexistence cases; residual magnitudes alone are not a universal existence test, especially as the bound vanishes at threshold.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximations of capillary menisci in polygonal channels
